title: A timestamp a client sends carries its UTC offset
intent: A date and time without a UTC offset names no instant: ten in the morning is a different moment in every zone. Stored as if it were UTC, it puts a sender in any other zone off by that zone's offset, and nothing reports it. The published API contract already rules such a value out, since a date-time there is the RFC 3339 form, whose offset is required. So the request boundary refuses one, in a request body and in a declared filter, and the refusal names the fix. Reading a value without an offset as UTC, for a sender known to send UTC without saying so, is the one way around it, and it is an escape a person decides and a reviewer sees.
reference: Each reference to terp.core's NaiveMeansUtc is refused: by name under any alias, through the terp.core module (core.NaiveMeansUtc), or inside a quoted annotation. Taking it is the opt-out marker on that line. A plain datetime field on a BaseSchema needs nothing, and neither does a datetime query parameter forwarded to a declared filter: at run time the schema refuses a client's timestamp text without an offset as a 422 at the field, and the filter refuses a bound without one as a 400 that names it (ADR 0206). A NaiveMeansUtc the file defines itself is not the escape, since the boundary does not step aside for it.

runtime.rationale: The request boundary holds the invariant itself. A request body built on BaseSchema refuses a client's timestamp text without a UTC offset before any field is validated, as a 422 located at the field, and a declared filter refuses a bound without an offset as a 400 that names the filter. The build-time half governs the one way around both, so taking it is never quiet.
